headline: A brisk, dry weekend follows the front; frost is likely in Central Kentucky Sunday morning while the Clemson area stays breezy and cool
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: Low clouds and a gusty north wind linger around Danville early today, but the region dries out and gradually brightens. Tonight turns clear and cold under high pressure. An official Frost Advisory covers Boyle County from 1–9 AM Sunday, and isolated freezing readings are possible in colder pockets. Sunday and Monday are sunny with a steady temperature recovery, though both nights remain chilly.

currentConditions.wind: North near 15 mph, gusting to 22 mph
currentConditions.precipitation: No precipitation reported in the latest observation; light rain and drizzle occurred earlier overnight

days.label: Saturday
days.hazard: OFFICIAL NWS ALERT: Frost Advisory for Boyle County from 1–9 AM Sunday. Independent concerns are north gusts around 20–30 mph today, widespread frost tonight and a localized freeze in colder pockets.
days.forecast: Low clouds around Danville thin through the morning while clouds linger longer toward the I-75 corridor. The afternoon becomes partly to mostly sunny, but a north wind keeps highs in the 50s. Winds ease quickly this evening as high pressure settles overhead. Clear skies and light wind then support a rapid temperature drop, widespread frost and isolated readings near or just below freezing by Sunday morning.

days.label: Sunday
days.hazard: OFFICIAL NWS ALERT: Frost Advisory remains in effect through 9 AM. Independent concern is widespread frost early, followed by another patchy frost risk Sunday night in sheltered locations.
days.forecast: Widespread frost during the early morning gives way to full sunshine. Light east winds and a modifying air mass allow highs to recover into the lower 60s. Sunday night remains clear and chilly; most towns stay above freezing, but colder rural valleys could fall into the lower 30s with patchy frost.

days.label: Monday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for Monday at issuance. Independent concern is patchy frost around daybreak in the coldest sheltered locations; no significant daytime hazard is expected.
days.forecast: Patchy frost is possible around daybreak, then sunny skies and light northeast winds bring a milder afternoon. Monday night remains clear and cool, but most locations should hold several degrees above freezing.

kentucky.bottomLine: Central Kentucky stays dry through Monday. Clouds break today, but a brisk north wind keeps temperatures in the 50s. Protect sensitive plants tonight: Boyle County is under a Frost Advisory, with isolated freezing temperatures possible. Sunny weather and gradual warming follow Sunday and Monday.
kentucky.confidence: High on the dry pattern and warming trend; high on frost, with moderate confidence on the exact extent of sub-freezing pockets

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson primary · Pickens County comparison
upstate.summary: The cold front is east of the Clemson–Central corridor. Clouds clear this morning, leaving a sunny, breezy and much cooler weekend. North winds remain gusty today, and northeast winds strengthen again Sunday. Clemson-area lows should generally remain in the upper 30s and 40s; official frost and freeze headlines are confined to the mountains and northern foothills outside the configured point.

days.label: Saturday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for the Clemson point. Independent concern is a gusty north wind, especially from late morning through afternoon; frost headlines are limited to mountain and northern-foothill zones outside the corridor.
days.forecast: Morning clouds quickly depart, leaving a sunny but sharply cooler day. North winds increase after sunrise, with gusts around 20–30 mph possible through the afternoon before easing this evening. Clear skies bring a chilly night, but the Clemson–Central corridor should generally remain above freezing; patchy frost is most plausible in sheltered colder locations north and west of town.

days.label: Sunday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for the Clemson point. Independent concern is another breezy northeast afternoon with gusts around 20–28 mph; widespread frost or a freeze is not expected in the corridor.
days.forecast: Sunny and cool with a persistent northeast wind. Gusts increase again during the afternoon, especially in exposed areas. Sunday night stays clear and chilly, but most Clemson and Central neighborhoods remain in the lower to middle 40s; colder sheltered spots may reach the upper 30s.

days.label: Monday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for the Clemson point, and no significant independent weather hazard is expected.
days.forecast: Sunny and milder as high pressure remains in control. Northeast winds are lighter than during the weekend. Monday night stays mostly clear with temperatures generally in the 40s.

upstate.bottomLine: The Upstate stays dry through Monday. Sunshine returns today, but north winds keep the weekend much cooler and breezy. Frost and freeze headlines apply to higher terrain outside Clemson and Central; the corridor itself should generally stay above freezing before a milder Monday.
upstate.confidence: High on dry weather and the weekend cool-down; moderate-high on peak gusts and localized sheltered-valley frost potential

sourceNotes: An official NWS Frost Advisory is active for Boyle County, Kentucky, from 1–9 AM EDT Sunday. No official NWS alert is active for the configured Clemson point; nearby mountain and northern-foothill frost/freeze headlines are outside the Clemson–Central corridor.

College of DuPage radar at 6:20 AM EDT showed no organized precipitation over Central Kentucky or the Clemson area; many weak circular echoes were non-meteorological ground clutter. True-color satellite at 6:16 AM showed the post-frontal cloud band shifting east with clearing spreading into the target regions.

The KDVK NWS observation record carried missing element values, so the contemporaneous official NOAA Aviation Weather METAR was used. KCEU had not reported since 4 PM EDT October 16, so current Upstate conditions use KLQK and KAND; KCEU remains a verification station when official data resume.

Official point forecasts, current observations, office discussions and multi-model guidance agree on a dry, much cooler weekend followed by gradual moderation; no unresolved material source conflict remains.
HRRR, RAP, NAM, NAM 3-km Nest, GFS, GEFS and ECMWF availability was verified from official run directories; College of DuPage panels supplied a common visual source.
Tempest data was not used for Upstate observations, verification, calibration or adjustment.
Official NWS alerts are separate from this independent analysis. Independent hazard probabilities do not constitute watches or warnings.
